page.layout: One printed page. Running head "EMBLEMA" centred at top, with page number 42 at upper left. Below it a full-width title "INTERIM PATITVR IVSTVS." Then a copperplate emblem engraving (hourglass hanging from a sunburst, a dog on a chain tied to a balance, scales and a broken arrow below). Below the engraving, a centred four-line verse in italic. In the right margin, at the foot, a catchword-like word "Multa" (a marginal note).

main_text.l: [Engraving: emblem picture, described under notes; no printed text in it.]
Quisquis in hoc Diui tractas præconia iuris
Æuo, hos in scopulos ingrediare, caue.
Æmulus ille Dei est qui ius dispensat & æquum

page.notes: The engraving shows an hourglass suspended from a radiant sun with stars, a dog tied by a chain to a yoke above, and a pair of scales with a sword and broken arrow on the ground. The verse line "Iusteziniustitiæ" reads as printed and is doubtful. The marginal word "Multa" stands at the lower right and is treated as a side note; it may be a catchword. Its placement and reading are uncertain.
